title: The Luka ripple
headline:
TWO PICKS.
TWO FUTURES.
subtitle: A draft-night exchange. Two careers. An afterlife nobody could have drawn up.
coverage: Traces Luka, Trae and the Dallas first through Reddish; the Reddish–Hart exchange joins the 2019 Davis branch. Follows New York’s first to Kris Murray and McCollum into Washington’s 2026 Trae exchange. Stops February 5, 2026. Other pick rights and secondary player branches are untraced.
takeaway: The draft-night package opens several paths. Follow one asset at a time.
imageAlt: Luka Dončić playing for Dallas in 2021

title: The night Dallas changed
headline:
ONE NIGHT.
TWO CORNERSTONES.
subtitle: Dirk’s draft rights. Garrity’s next stop. The separate deal that brought Nash.
coverage: Follows the separate Dirk and Nash draft-night packages, Dallas’s 1999 first to Marion, and Marion through Miami and Toronto back to Dallas in July 2009. Shaq’s Miami, Phoenix and Cleveland exchanges are shared intersections. Conditional Toronto picks and other branches stop at their recorded transfers; Nash’s free agency is not a trade return.
takeaway: Pat Garrity’s rights connect the two deals. Each package still matters.
imageAlt: Dirk Nowitzki playing for Dallas in 2009

title: Brooklyn buys the present
headline:
THE LONG
GAME.
subtitle: Three firsts, one swap, and the patience between a promise and a player.
coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
takeaway: A swap is a right to exchange picks. Boston still needed another trade to reach No. 3.
imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

title: Thirteen to Los Angeles
headline:
BEFORE
THE LEGEND.
subtitle: A draft selection in Charlotte. A rights transfer two weeks later.
coverage: The June 26 selection and July 11, 1996 Bryant–Divac exchange only. This is a short origin story; later free agency is outside the trade graph.
takeaway: Draft night and the effective trade date are not always the same day.

title: The dynasty splits
headline:
THE BIG
AFTERLIFE.
subtitle: From Shaq’s move to Miami to two very different Gasol destinations.
coverage: Follows both Shaq pick returns, Marion’s Dallas route, Butler’s Dallas exchange, the Gasol packages, and the Lakers 2010 first through Vásquez to Powell rights, Anunoby and Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. Untraced obligations are labelled; no free agency or shared championship is treated as a trade connection.
takeaway: The connection runs through whole packages, with additional assets entering each time.

title: The brothers in the fine print
headline:
A TALE OF
TWO GASOLS.
subtitle: One brother headlines the trade. The other appears as draft rights.
coverage: Follows Marc to Toronto and the Lakers 2010 first to Vásquez, then his New Orleans, Sacramento, Toronto and Milwaukee exchanges. The Clippers first becomes Anunoby; the later Knicks package’s Detroit second becomes Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. The Lakers 2008 first and other side branches remain untraced.
takeaway: A draft-rights entry in one deal can become the headliner of another.

title: Boston’s two big swings
headline:
ALL IN.
THEN RESET.
subtitle: The 2007 arrival and the 2013 departure belong to different Boston bets.
coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
takeaway: Returning a team’s own pick obligation extinguishes a claim; it creates no extra pick.
imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

title: Houston finds its headliner
headline:
THE BET
ON THIRTEEN.
subtitle: The player went to Houston. Three very different draft promises went the other way.
coverage: From Houston’s 2012 acquisition through the completed 2021 four-team exchange and 2022 Philadelphia deal. Selected pick branches become Adams, Abrines, McGary, Eason, Nembhard, Ben Sheppard and Reed Sheppard. Stops June 26, 2024; later player moves, swap amendments and unused fallback terms are untraced.
takeaway: A protected pick can survive one draft and convey at the next. It is still one obligation.

title: The return trip
headline:
A LEAP.
A LOOP.
subtitle: Kawhi goes north. Years later, Poeltl’s branch circles back to Toronto.
coverage: Follows Keldon Johnson and Poeltl’s return, then Toronto’s No. 8 into the Dillingham rights trade. Stops June 26, 2024 with Minnesota’s future first and swap outstanding at that point.
takeaway: A returning player can open a new branch years after the original exchange.

title: The price of right now
headline:
FIVE FIRSTS.
ONE FUTURE.
subtitle: George arrives in Oklahoma City, then leaves in a very different kind of deal.
coverage: Both sides of Indiana’s George return are followed: Sabonis into the Haliburton package; Oladipo through the four-team Harden deal, LeVert, Nembhard and Ben Sheppard. Includes the full Clippers package and Jalen Williams. Stops June 22, 2023; other picks and intervening free agency are untraced.
takeaway: Shai and the draft obligations arrive in the same package. Their later paths remain distinct.

title: The Davis chain
headline:
THREE CITIES.
THREE DEALS.
subtitle: New Orleans to Los Angeles. Dallas to Washington. Follow the actual packages.
coverage: The Davis route from 2019 through February 2026, plus Hart into the Reddish exchange and New York’s first into Kris Murray. McCollum’s New Orleans–Washington–Atlanta path is included, as is Chicago’s second through Washington to Dallas. Other rights are untraced beyond their displayed transactions.
takeaway: Washington appears in the first deal as a facilitator and in the last as Davis’s destination.

title: Another Dallas crossroads
headline:
TWO STARS.
MORE THREADS.
subtitle: Kyrie’s arrival includes Markieff Morris. Follow the less obvious thread.
coverage: Follows Morris from the Kyrie package into the Luka deal, then Davis into Washington. This is not a claim that Kyrie was traded for any of those returns. Brooklyn’s picks are untraced.
takeaway: Shared teammates can connect trades whose headline players never change hands for one another.

title: Four days in Portland
headline:
THE HOLIDAY
DETOUR.
subtitle: Dame moves to Milwaukee. Jrue’s Portland stop turns out to be very short.
coverage: Includes Brogdon’s 2022 Boston arrival as backward context for the 2023 Holiday package, then Lillard’s three-team trade, Holiday to Boston and the July 7, 2025 Simons exchange. Future draft rights and other player branches are untraced.
takeaway: The final 2025 exchange contains no draft picks; early reports described a different proposal.

title: A new center of gravity
headline:
BIG MAN.
BIGGER PACKAGE.
subtitle: The New York–Minnesota headline has a Charlotte chapter, too.
coverage: The complete October 2, 2024 three-team trade and Detroit’s first conveying to Minnesota as No. 17 in 2025. Other players and second-round outcomes are untraced.
takeaway: The original franchise of a traded pick can be a team that did not participate in this deal.

title: Five teams, one headline
headline:
THE FIVE-TEAM
SHUFFLE.
subtitle: A deadline blockbuster whose edges reach far beyond Miami and Golden State.
coverage: The final February 6 five-team package and the Golden State first becoming Miami’s No. 20. Some minor second-round terms were undisclosed; those assets are labelled and left untraced.
takeaway: A headline is an entry point. The full exchange is the story.
